evidence.claim: Model risk score 0.79. In the 0.70-0.85 band the bank's closed history holds 817 confirmed frauds against 234 cleared alarms, a likelihood ratio of 0.67 - mildly exculpatory, consistent with the dataset note that above 0.70 most flagged transactions turn out to be legitimate

$292.36 is 7.9x this card's median and above its 95th percentile. Counter-intuitively this is mildly exculpatory: large outliers appear on 16% of cleared alarms and 6% of confirmed fraud, because confirmed fraud tends to stay inside the cardholder's normal range to avoid attention
The bank has 1 confirmed-fraud case(s) already closed on this card (CC-4160), pattern(s): card_not_present_fraud

External email-domain intelligence classifies 'hotmail.com' as a free webmail address, which is what most real cardholders and most fraudsters both use. Measured across the bank's closed cases this is the baseline -- it appears on 3,667 confirmed frauds and 573 cleared alarms -- so it is named as context and carries no weight.

Connected components place this card in the graph's giant device-sharing component (2,500 cards). Transitive device sharing percolates at every threshold tested, so membership is not evidence of a ring and carries no weight here; it is recorded because policy R6 asks for the shared element to be named.

Known fraud pattern 2: Card-not-present fraud: Card-not-present fraud. The number is used online without the card. Amounts and products that don't fit the cardholder's history, often in a burst of two to four within 48 hours. On its own, one unusual online purchase is ambiguous: verify. Policy R1 to R4.

Policy rule R1: Verify before you block on a weak signal: R1. Verify before you block on a weak signal. If the case rests on a single signal (including a risk score alone) and your assessed fraud probability is below 0.70, recommend `VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER` or `STEP_UP_AUTH` before any block. Blocking a legitimate customer on one signal is a policy breach.
